answer: Unique answer commitments bind each registration to a fresh answer string whose hash is stored and rejected on reuse. A new identity must solve a challenge seeded by that answer and a spiral of prior block hashes, yielding a nonce valid only for its string. Even a copied sonnet fails the seed check because its answer hash already exists. The attacker pays about 2^22 sequential hashes plus storage per identity, and any mirror of an existing answer is rejected.
